title: Shinbo / SHAFT-style flat graphics: title cards, Mincho x gothic, red-black-white flats, architecture, paper collage
summary: Full-screen title cards on one flat ground (black, paper white or signal red), high-contrast Mincho display against small gothic numbers, symmetric corridors or extreme offsets, cut-paper collage that never covers copy, and a flash-hold-black cutting rhythm.

provenance.experiment: Nocturne Corridor (夜想回廊), an original fictional anime set made to test style grammar + materials + templates in one round: 14 title cards, a poster, two web screens, a game UI screen and a 13.9 s cut film, saved as a first pass and a reviewed final.
provenance.method: Grammar written before the first pass (the style's established answer: title cards, Mincho x gothic collision, flat red/black/white, architecture and void, Inukare-style collage, flash/hold rhythm); measurements from the browser check and colour statistics of both rounds.
measured: First pass: 13 contrast failures, 1 vertical line off the canvas, 2 texts under a collage key; 3 of 4 changes between rounds were these mechanical problems, 3 places needed taste.
Final: 0 contrast, 0 off-canvas, 0 collage over copy; main colours about 74% of pixels; hue spread of coloured pixels under 5 degrees (almost only red).
Japanese OFL Mincho fonts (Shippori Mincho B1, Zen Old Mincho) lack simplified-only hanzi (钥 证 记 间); Noto Serif CJK SC covers them.
provenance.fixtures: tests/fixtures/style-pack-shinbo (first-pass and final pages with subset fonts and downscaled CC0 collage)

black.use: ink black: black cards, architecture lines, text on paper (16:1)

paper.use: paper white: white cards, text on black or red (4.8:1 on red, any size)

red.use: signal red: third main colour and focus; text in red on black only at 24px or more (3.5:1)

red_deep.use: shadow side of red flats only; no text

grey.use: decoration and small numbers on black (5.2:1)

accent.use: one jarring accent per piece (teal; magenta #E4007F or yellow #FFE100 as alternatives); only black text on it (white is 2.6:1)

display.use: giant single characters, shared-glyph display words (夜, 蝶, 回廊, 第〇夜); switches whole strings to Noto Serif CJK SC when a simplified-only character is missing

ruby.use: ruby-style readings, only on flat grounds

num.use: numbers, codes, Latin capitals, colliding against Mincho

fonts.licence: All roles use SIL OFL 1.1 fonts.
fonts.note: Fonts are named, not bundled. Give --font-dir <dir> to render to read their coverage (whole-string switching) and embed them for --png and the browser check; without it the stacks are written as named and coverage is reported as unknown.

grammar: Title card: one flat ground for the whole frame, one or two text groups; a single character may fill or exceed the frame height (data-bleed).
Small text sits in the corner farthest from the big text, tracked .3-.5em.
Vertical for sentences, horizontal for numbers and titles; brackets 「」『』 up to twice the text size, in red.
Composition is either centred and symmetric (corridor) or extremely offset (one column of text and 60% void).
Tilt only objects and text blocks (-4 to -38 degrees), never figures.
Web and UI: a red vertical or horizontal bar carries navigation; hover is an inverted block with a hard shadow shift, never a fade or gradient.

procedural: one-point corridor, stairs, window grid, checker floor (drawn by the layouts: corridor() in layouts-shinbo.cjs)
cut-paper objects: butterfly, key, gear, flower, eye, scissors, door (SVG with a paper edge and one soft shadow, filter cut)
screentone dots (pattern), paper multiply overlay, ink grain, print misregistration
collage: Objects as cut stickers (paper edge about 1.4% plus a soft shadow); plates as hand-cut polygons with a white edge; ink as pure-alpha ink when tinted.
Per image: 1 main object (largest, may tilt), 2-3 secondary objects, at least 1 procedural cut-paper shape.
Collage never covers copy (browser rule collage-cover); the focus (the red door at the end of the corridor) is never covered.
Engravings (grey) next to flats stay mid-tone and never sit under text.
materials.sources: Public-domain and CC0 engravings and botanical plates (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access, The Met Open Access); the material source catalog of issue #287 lists and cuts them. Image slots take your files; nothing is bundled except the test fixtures' downscaled pieces.

motion.blackFlash: a black of 2-6 frames between two flashes is a black flash inside the group, not a separator
motion.groundsInFlashGroup: one ground tone per flash group: cards in a group share the ground and vary by text, crop or push-in, so the cut does not strobe

flashLimit.note: a cut-list approximation after the WCAG 2.3.1 general-flash definition, on each card's mean luminance (or its ground tone); not a photosensitivity verdict: the encoded-film check (verify film-render) is authoritative

motion.sound: a 12 ms noise click on each flash cut, a 52 Hz thud on holds

checks.note: The browser check runs on every render of this style (contrast against the ground with the text hidden, 10th percentile; overlap by ink; collage by alpha pixels; whole-string glyph coverage).
